summary: Paraguay’s restoration pledges include 187,942 ha of energy and timber forest plantations by 2030—about 1.1% of the country’s 42.5% forest cover—plus 4,588 ha of forest restoration by 2030, 50 ha of protective forest and two pilot restoration projects by 2035. Conservation targets include a 15–18% increase in protected wildlife areas and protection of at least 20% of national territory by 2030, with 10% effectively managed; fire-prevention work also reaches 75% of rural educational institutions by 2035. Agricultural measures reach 50% of small-scale cattle farmers, reduce nitrogen fertilizer use by 5–10%, use efficient rice varieties on 30% of the 2030 area, and expand direct seeding by 20% against a projected 3.9 million ha surface. The 6,536.3 ha agroforestry pledge is ≈0.07% of current agriculture. Mixed measures add a 60% certified-forest increase to 72,323 ha, two wetland projects, four stream interventions and eight-department agroforestry.
